name: Chloroform
about: Points sampled from the source of each property record (or the source's own tabulated values) by validation/python/fit_properties.py. test/properties.test.js checks that the coefficients in src/data/components.json reproduce them within the maximum deviation stated in each record.

source.name: ChemSep v8.3 pure-component database
source.reference: Kooijman and Taylor, ChemSep v8.3, chemsep1.xml (2021), via https://github.com/DanWBR/dwsim (DWSIM.Thermodynamics/Assets/Databases)
source.fit: ChemSep equation 105 coefficients taken over unchanged except: Tmin raised to the triple point 209.63 K (ChemSep: 209.00 K). A converted from kmol/m3 to kg/m3 with the ChemSep molar mass 119.3776 kg/kmol.; reproduces ChemSep within 0.0001 % at 200 points 209.63-535.95 K
source.chain: CoolProp 8.0.0: fluid not included; NIST WebBook: no data
source.measuredCheck: NIST TRC ThermoML Archive (validation/python/check_measured.py): 107 measured values from 32 articles, 273.1-323.1 K; median deviation of the articles 0.85 % (within the 1 % tolerance of the engineering report); largest single deviation +1.49 % at 298.1 K (Shekaari 2010, doi:10.1021/je100369a); docs/MEASURED_CHECKS.md

source.name: NIST Chemistry WebBook
source.reference: Chase M.W., Jr., NIST-JANAF Thermochemical Tables, Fourth Edition, J. Phys. Chem. Ref. Data, Monograph 9 (1998) 1-1951, Shomate equation as given in the NIST Chemistry WebBook (SRD 69), gas phase thermochemistry data
source.fit: 200 points sampled from the Shomate equation, 298.00-1200.00 K, max deviation 0.095 %
source.notes: Shomate equation Cp = A + B t + C t^2 + D t^3 + E/t^2, t = T/1000, range 298-1200 K (JANAF data last reviewed in December 1968).
